newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-KOMEN TO ATTACK TWO MILES MARK..
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KOMEN TO ATTACK TWO MILES MARK..

text.p: Daniel Komen of Kenya will attempt to regain the world best mark for two miles in Belgium this month despite recent health problems, a spokesman for his agent said on Wednesday.

Komen, holder of the 3,000 metres world best time, finished a disappointing fourth in a 5,000 metres in Stockholm on Monday. He will race in Hechtel on July 19 when he hopes to become the first man to run the two miles in under eight minutes.
"Daniel felt ill last week -- we still don't know what it was -- and then had an allergic reaction to the aspirin he took," the spokesman said.
"That's the reason for his below-par performances in Oslo and Stockholm. He didn't run like he usually does.
"However, we think he should be okay to run in Hechtel, which will be his last race before the world championships."
Komen set a two miles world mark of 8:03.54 in July 1996 but Ethiopia's Haile Gebrselassie lowered it to 8:01.08 in May this year.
Komen is favourite to win the 5,000 metres at the world championships in Athens in August.
